newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico City subway subsidies to remain through '97.
newsitem.headline: Mexico City subway subsidies to remain through '97.

text.p: Government subsidies for Mexico City's subway system will remain in place through 1997 and will thereafter be withdrawn gradually, the director general of the transport system said Monday.

Alfonso Caso told reporters the withdrawl of subsidies, currently running at 60 percent, would imply an "adjustment" in the tariffs for the subway. The largely underground train network is known in Mexico as the metro and is one of the cheapest transport systems in the world.
Around 4.6 million people use the metro daily. They pay a flat-rate one peso (13 cents) for each journey irrespective of the distance they travel.
